claims.text: A conventional elemental Cr coating on zirconium-alloy cladding is prone to Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
An Inconel 718 transition layer can be deposited between zirconium alloy and elemental Cr as a thin interlayer.
The nickel-based transition layer will inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The transition layer will improve coating mechanical durability under normal operating and accident conditions.
The transition layer will improve oxidation durability under both normal operating and accident conditions.
The nickel-based transition layer promotes a graded interface.
The transition layer and adjacent materials have well-matched thermal expansion coefficients.
The nickel-based transition layer acts as a diffusion barrier that limits direct transport between Cr and zirconium alloy.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will maintain a distinct separation between the Cr coating and zirconium substrate.
Maintaining interfacial separation will reduce premature coating failure caused by interfacial alloy formation.
An Inconel 718 transition layer can alleviate interfacial stress concentration.
Reduced thermal stress will reduce cracking or spallation in the Cr-on-zirconium coating system.
Compared with unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the modified coating will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Compared with unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the modified coating will exhibit improved interfacial mechanical integrity.
Compared with unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the modified coating will exhibit enhanced oxidation resistance in moderate-temperature water and high-temperature steam.
The proposed benefit applies at approximately 290°C during long-term PWR-water exposure and at 1200–1600°C during short steam exposure.
Quantitative long-term data for this nickel-barrier/Cr/zirconium system in extreme nuclear environments are limited.
Three-point bending and thermal tensile testing can quantitatively assess interfacial bonding strength in multilayer coatings.
